parameters.jsonBody:
={{ JSON.stringify({ contents: [{ role: 'user', parts: [{ text: "You are an expert technical recruiter, ATS optimization specialist, LaTeX CV writer and cover letter writer.
Inputs below: a job offer, the detected letter language and work mode, the candidate's projects catalog (JSON) and the candidate's LaTeX CV. The original CV and the projects catalog are the ONLY source of truth about the candidate (the "real repository").

PROCESS (do it silently, do not output it):
A. Analyze the offer: job title, company, location, work mode, experience level, education, programming languages, frameworks, databases, cloud, DevOps, tools, methodologies, responsibilities, domain, soft skills, language requirements.
B. If a web search tool is available, run 1 to 3 short searches (similar job offers, technologies really asked for this role, representative portfolio projects, the company's technical context) to understand which of the candidate's REAL projects are the most representative of the role. Web results never allow you to invent anything about the candidate.
C. Classify the offer keywords, identify the target profile, match the catalog projects, then write the CV and the letter.

ABSOLUTE RULE - NEVER INVENT: no experience, company, client, project, technology, framework, language, certification, degree, responsibility, metric, result, production deployment or expertise level that is not in the real repository. A technology asked by the offer but absent from the repository is a SKILL GAP: never add it to the CV (not in the title, Profile, Experience, Projects or Skills) and never claim it in the letter. The certification "AWS Certified AI Practitioner" stays in Certifications but does NOT prove any AWS service skill (EC2, S3, RDS, Lambda, VPC, IAM, ECS, EKS, CloudWatch...). Never merge two projects into one, never create a project, never add a technology to a project because the offer asks for it.
POSITIONING: the candidate is a Computer Science and Networks Engineer (EMSI, 2026) with a Master 2 in AI (2026). Never describe him as student, junior, intern, final-year student, undergraduate or currently studying, and never as senior, lead, manager, principal or architect.

===KEYWORDS=== RULES:
Keywords describe the OFFER (include them even when the candidate lacks them). ALWAYS write them in ENGLISH, whatever the language of the offer: translate French terms into the standard English technical term (e.g. "bases vectorielles" -> "vector databases", "evaluation de modeles" -> "model evaluation", "conteneurisation" -> "containerization", "securite" -> "security"); keep product names unchanged. Use short concrete terms, ONE term per item (e.g. "EC2", "Docker", "CI/CD", never "Python or Bash"), 3 to 8 items per list, comma-separated. MUST_HAVE = explicitly required skills; IMPORTANT = main responsibilities and strongly desired skills; NICE_TO_HAVE = pluses; DOMAIN_KEYWORDS = business domain terms.

cv_latex RULES:
1. The complete, compilable LaTeX source, from \documentclass to \end{document}. No Markdown code fences. Keep exactly the same preamble, packages, macros, geometry, spacing and fonts; never add \vspace, never add a photo. Keep the same sections in the same order: header, Profile, Professional Experience, Projects & Portfolio, Technical Skills, Education, Certifications, Availability.
2. Header: the name line unchanged; the title line adapted to the offer's job title, in English, honest and consistent with the real profile ("Ingenieur DevOps" -> "DevOps Engineer", "Developpeur Full Stack" -> "Full Stack Developer", "Ingenieur BI" -> "Business Intelligence / Data Engineer", "AI Engineer" -> "AI Engineer"); a short specialization after " -- " is allowed only with real skills. Contact line: phone and email unchanged; location: if the offer's city is Casablanca keep "Casablanca, Morocco", otherwise write "Casablanca, Morocco (open to <offer city>)". Never add an address, LinkedIn, GitHub, Portfolio or photo to the header.
3. Profile: at most 50 words (3 lines), written for THIS offer. Its first words are the target job title. Highlight the most relevant real experience and technologies, use the offer's keywords naturally (only those the candidate really has), no generic wording.
4. Professional Experience: keep every entry, employer, position title and date exactly. You MAY rephrase and reorder the bullet points, use the offer's vocabulary, stronger action verbs and highlight existing technologies, but every statement must be supported by the original CV or the projects catalog. Keep at most the same number of bullet points per entry, each at most 2 lines (about 28 words).
5. Projects & Portfolio: keep its introductory GitHub line, then 2 projects chosen from the PROJECTS CATALOG that best match the offer (category_tags, technologies, description, keywords, responsibilities, web research); a 3rd project only if each of the three fits on a single line. For each: the catalog name in bold (it may be shortened), a reformulated description based only on its catalog description, highlighting what matters for the offer, then in italics at most 6 technologies taken ONLY from that project's catalog "technologies" list. Each project at most 2 lines. If the offer is mainly an AI / machine learning / generative AI position, do not select "RAG Knowledge Assistant (PFE-RAG)" (it would duplicate the RAG work of the Qualitiz experience).
6. Technical Skills: exactly 5 bullet lines, each at most 1.5 lines. Reorder categories and items so the skills most relevant to the offer come first; category names may be adapted to the offer. Use ONLY skills present in the real repository; never add a skill gap.
7. Education and Certifications: unchanged.
8. Availability: start with "Based in Casablanca, Morocco. Available immediately"; if the offer's city is not Casablanca continue with " for a position in <offer city>"; if the "=== WORK MODE ===" section is not "none", add that the candidate is open to that work mode. Never claim to live in another city.
9. ONE PAGE: the CV must fit on one A4 page; apart from the Projects items you add, the rewritten CV must not be longer than the original.
10. The CV is always in English. Escape LaTeX special characters correctly (write \& for an ampersand, never a bare &).

cover_letter RULES:
1. Language: the one given in "=== LETTER LANGUAGE ===". Length: 180 to 220 words in total.
2. Structure: a salutation line, then EXACTLY 4 paragraphs separated by blank lines, then a short closing formula line and the name "Haimoudi Nouaman" on the last line.
   Paragraph 1 - HOOK: start directly with a concrete fact about the role, a technology, the product, a project or the company context (quote the exact job title and the company name).
   Paragraph 2 - PROOF: ONE real accomplishment matching the main MUST_HAVE, from the experience or a catalog project, with its real technologies.
   Paragraph 3 - FIT: link the profile to ONE concrete responsibility of the offer (name it). Mention the offer's city honestly: the candidate is based in Casablanca; if the city differs, say he is ready to work in that city; if the work mode is not "none", mention it in the same sentence. Never claim to live elsewhere.
   Paragraph 4 - CLOSING: short, professional and confident; propose an interview.
3. Never claim a skill gap, never overstate, never mention an attachment other than the CV.
4. FORBIDDEN phrases (and any equivalent): "Je vous ecris pour", "vif interet", "Je suis actuellement", "Je souhaite vous exprimer", "Actuellement etudiant", "Fort de mon experience", "Je reste a votre entiere disposition", "Je me tiens a votre disposition", "Je serais ravi de", "N'hesitez pas a me contacter", "Passionne par l'innovation", "Je vous prie d'agreer", "Veuillez agreer", "I am writing to", "express my interest", "Currently a student", "I am currently studying", "As a final-year student", "I would be delighted", "Please do not hesitate to contact me".
5. Plain text; no Markdown symbols, no placeholders like [Company].

=== JOB OFFER ===
" + 'Title: ' + $json.job_title + '
Company: ' + $json.company + '
Location: ' + $json.location + '

Description:
' + $json.description + '

=== LETTER LANGUAGE (detected from the job offer text) ===
' + ((($json.description || '').match(/ (le|la|les|des|et|vous|votre|pour|avec|une|du|nous|est|dans|sur) /gi) || []).length > (($json.description || '').match(/ (the|and|you|your|for|with|our|is|are|to|of|in|we) /gi) || []).length ? 'French' : 'English') + '

=== WORK MODE (detected from the job offer text) ===
' + $json.work_mode + '

=== PROJECTS CATALOG (JSON) ===
' + JSON.stringify($json.projects, null, 2) + '

=== ORIGINAL CV (LaTeX) ===
' + $json.cv_latex + '

' + "OUTPUT FORMAT (mandatory, identical for every model): plain text only, exactly the structure below, nothing before the first marker and nothing after the last one. Write the LaTeX raw, exactly as in a .tex file, with real line breaks, not escaped, no code fences.
===KEYWORDS===
MUST_HAVE:
<keyword1, keyword2, ...>
IMPORTANT:
<keyword1, keyword2, ...>
NICE_TO_HAVE:
<keyword1, keyword2, ...>
DOMAIN_KEYWORDS:
<keyword1, keyword2, ...>
===CV_LATEX===
<complete LaTeX source>
===COVER_LETTER===
<cover letter>
===END===" }] }], generationConfig: { temperature: 0.2 } }) }}

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify(Object.assign({}, $json, { url: $('Webhook').first().json.query.url, job_title: $('Extraire offre').first().json.job_title, company: $('Extraire offre').first().json.company, location: $('Extraire offre').first().json.location })) }}
